solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Breathing aids, no less, when swimming around outside of rock

indicators.note: to sit around something is to enclose it, so one set of letters wraps another
letters that are swimming are moving about freely, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two ends, so only the edge letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A diver insists on breathing gear while swimming around the edge of a rocky outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside of rock' means the word's edge letters, not something outside a rock; 'no less' sounds like emphasis but is the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorkels are tubes that let a swimmer take in air with the face underwater.

clue.text: Lana is confused about time of birth

indicators.note: to be about something is to go round it, so one piece surrounds another
something confused is muddled up, so its letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman named Lana is muddled about when she was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of birth' reads as one phrase, but the setter splits it: 'time' is the inserted letter and 'of birth' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective describing anything relating to being born, as in a natal chart or prenatal care.

clue.text: Beam from top of roof, indeed

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
ay is an old or dialect form of yes, an emphatic agreement like 'indeed'

explanation.surface: Someone notices a beam of light coming from the very top of a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' suggests a wooden roof timber, which fits the surface, but here it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a narrow line of light or radiation, which is one sense of a beam.

clue.text: Register put up in hall, or nearby

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: a run of consecutive letters across the end of one word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A notice-board register is pinned up in the hall or close to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters LORNE run from the end of 'hall' through 'or' into 'nearby'; read upwards they give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or enter one's name on a list, which is what registering means.

clue.text: Cake ingredient for ruler's wife

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pale seedless dried grape used in baking
second meaning: the consort of a Muslim sovereign

explanation.surface: A recipe note: some baking ingredient is set aside for the monarch's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cake baked for a queen; instead the two phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dried golden grape found in fruit cakes and the wife of a sultan.

clue.text: It hurts removing penny from purse!

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a pouch is a small bag for carrying money, like a purse
p is the standard abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone complains that taking even a penny out of their purse is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It hurts' is the definition, standing for the exclamation itself; the exclamation mark points at a cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the cry a person gives when something causes sudden pain, so it expresses 'it hurts'.

clue.text: Land alone prepared for absolutely everyone

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lands a plane solo, ready to impress everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land alone' looks like an instruction to a pilot, but its nine letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning every single person without exception, as in a greeting to all present.

clue.text: Loudly applauded old guerrilla, European socialist

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary of the 1950s and 60s
E is the abbreviation for European
red is a common label for a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A crowd noisily applauds a veteran guerrilla fighter who is a European socialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old guerrilla' is Che Guevara, a stock crossword figure; the list of descriptions is three separate pieces placed in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to shout approval, so being cheered means receiving noisy applause.

clue.text: Remain a year on street

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the second-named piece leads

parts.note: St is the standard abbreviation for street
taken as written
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone decides to live on the same street for another year.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'A on B' puts A after B, so the street abbreviation comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to keep on being there rather than leave, the same as remaining.

clue.text: No longer anxious, if somehow ever idle

indicators.note: 'somehow' means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worrier would finally stop fretting if they could ever manage to be idle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like advice about relaxing; 'ever idle' simply supplies eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relieved means feeling the release of worry once a feared outcome has passed.

clue.text: Large amount coming in to replenish a small fleet

indicators.note: something coming in to another enters it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to replenish is to fill up again
a lot is a large quantity
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large shipment arrives to restock a small naval squadron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replenish a' looks like it governs the fleet, but 'a small fleet' splits: 'a' joins the wordplay and 'small fleet' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a modest group of boats or small warships, smaller than a full naval fleet.

clue.text: Glower when tense, harbouring a mild disease

indicators.note: a harbour shelters ships within it, so harbouring means holding something inside

parts.note: tense muscles or ropes are tight
taken as written
an ill is an ailment, here a minor one

explanation.surface: Someone scowls whenever they're tense from carrying a minor illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' normally means scowl; here it is read as 'glow-er', a thing that glows, which a rear lamp on a car does.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle, a thing that glows in the dark, jokingly called a glow-er.

clue.text: Spy name attached to ancient vessel

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
Noah's Ark, the boat of the Bible story

explanation.surface: An agent's code name is linked to an old ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Nark is British slang for a police informer, someone who spies and tells.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is an informer who secretly watches and reports on others, which is close to a spy.

clue.text: Behold desire to be rather mean

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Observe a wish to be somewhat stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests stingy, but here it means low in quality or status, and 'rather' supplies the -ish ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of poor or base matches low, and the suffix -ish softens it to 'somewhat'.

clue.text: A single broadcast recalled in the past

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective meaning former

parts.note: one is a single unit

indicators.note: to call something back is to send it the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to broadcast a signal is to emit it

explanation.surface: A single programme broadcast long ago is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests memory, which suits 'in the past', but it turns the broadcast word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, describing something that was so at an earlier period but is no longer.

clue.text: Is in possession of the chap's hard drug

parts.note: to have something is to possess it
belonging to a man
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A man is caught carrying hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard drug' reads as one phrase, but 'hard' gives a letter and 'drug' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, a narcotic smoked or eaten for its effects.

clue.text: Ace was crossing road to get prizes

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: something crossing another lies across it, so here one word straddles another

parts.note: taken as written
Rd is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A star performer was walking across a road to collect trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing road' paints a pedestrian, but it tells one word to straddle another.
explanation.definitionFit: Awards are honours or trophies given for achievement, the same as prizes.

clue.text: Musical instrument's endless beauty

indicators.note: without an end, so the word's final letter is cut off

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: An instrument is praised for its limitless beauty of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'instrument' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is a hollow metal percussion instrument that rings when struck, used in orchestras and churches.

clue.text: Bob and Carol crossing small mountain

indicators.note: something crossing another lies across it, so here one word straddles another

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
a hill is a low mountain

explanation.surface: Two friends, Bob and Carol, hike over a little peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and Carol look like two people; Bob is old British slang for a shilling, a pre-1971 coin worth five pence, and Carol is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob was the everyday British slang name for the shilling coin, twelve old pence.

clue.text: Popular period for renting property in bay

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
in British usage a let is a period during which a property is rented

explanation.surface: Summer is the busy rental season for holiday homes by the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: A let is the British term for a lease or rental period on a house or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a small arm of the sea reaching into the coast, which is a kind of bay.

clue.text: Approaches RN sea exercises

indicators.note: exercises put things through their paces, working the letters into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval vessel draws close during Royal Navy manoeuvres at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy; 'Approaches' looks like a noun but is the verb, and 'exercises' is not a noun either.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to come closer to it, which is what approaching means.

clue.text: Some stirring dialogue: one way to tell Times from Sun!

definitions.text: one way to tell Times from Sun

indicators.note: 'some' means a part of, so only a portion of the letters is taken

parts.note: a run of letters across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A rousing speech compares The Times newspaper with The Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times and the Sun look like rival newspapers, but they are the time of day and the sun itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring dial is a portable sundial shaped like a ring, which reads the hour from the sun's light through a small hole.

clue.text: Advance unaccompanied, according to report

indicators.note: a report is something heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: lone means on one's own, without company

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward alone, so the news story says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' looks like a verb about going forward; here it is a noun, money paid out ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is a sum of money lent or paid early, which is a loan.

clue.text: Clue not regularly seen as sign

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A crossword clue that crops up only now and then is taken as a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not regularly' looks like one phrase meaning occasionally, but 'not' is part of the letters to be thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac used in astrology.

clue.text: Fresh, right after exercising

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
rt is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Feeling refreshed straight after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' suggests invigorated, but it means cheeky; 'after' places the right abbreviation behind the exercise one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in the sense of impudent or forward matches pert, meaning cheeky and saucy.

clue.text: Place for plants: you no longer would have means to water them outside

indicators.note: one thing outside another is wrapped round it, so these letters go round the rest

parts.note: a hose is used for watering plants
thou is the old, no longer used form of you

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a greenhouse saves them from carrying water to plants outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You no longer' looks like part of a sentence about gardening, but it means an archaic form of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is a heated greenhouse where tender plants are grown out of season.
